messages.subject: Getting extremely low density estimates
parts:
Hi guys!

I've got some data on amazonian toucan species, which my tutor has put into distance for me, and I'm trying to estimate density per species. However, I'm getting extremely small estimates some as small as 0.006 per sq km. The highest results I'm getting are for a species of which 311 were recorded and those range from 0.1 per sq km to 0.3. The species for which 0.006 was estimated had only 47 recordings over 5 habitats so I guess the small sample size could be the problem? Not sure if there's anything I can do about this but my tutor has stopped replying to me so have come here in search of help as I am extremely new to program distance. 

Hope someone can offer me some advice, and thanks in advance!
Johny A

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Getting extremely low density estimates
parts:
Johny

The first thing to check when things look unusual is that you have all the proper units for measurements.  What units were distances measured?  What distances were transects measured?  This is particularly troublesome of you did not collect the data yourself.

If you are using Distance as a stand-alone program, you specify the names of the units used, and the software makes appropriate conversions.  If you are using the R package Distance, you must make those conversions yourself using the argument "convert.units" in the function ds().
